issue.standard_remedy: Consolidate tail suppliers into preferred suppliers
issue.summary: 121 of 161 suppliers share the last 20% of category spend

plan.diagnosis: Severe supplier fragmentation in Copper wire & bar category with an HHI of 450 (indicating very low concentration) and 121 of 161 suppliers sharing only 20% of spend ($10,804,723), averaging $89,295 per tail supplier. The top supplier (Horizon United Metals AG) holds only 12.6% share, demonstrating lack of strategic leverage and excessive administrative overhead across multiple ERPs.

remedy_steps.step: Conduct tail supplier analysis to identify the 121 suppliers with transaction counts below 4 per year or spend below $50,000, then issue RFQ to Horizon United Metals AG and 2-3 other qualified strategic suppliers for volume consolidation

Negotiate volume-based pricing with selected strategic suppliers targeting 15-20% savings on the $10,804,723 tail spend through consolidation, establishing preferred supplier agreements with tiered pricing

Execute supplier rationalization by blocking 90-100 tail suppliers across all ERPs (SAP LFA1/LFB1 posting block flag, Oracle EBS 'Inactive' status, Dynamics 365 'Hold' status, NetSuite 'Inactive', Coupa supplier deactivation) while maintaining 25-30 tactical suppliers for specialty requirements

Implement approved vendor lists (AVLs) and source lists in SAP (ME01), Oracle EBS (Approved Supplier List), and Dynamics 365, restricting PO creation to 3-5 preferred suppliers for 80% of copper wire & bar volume
Deploy requisition catalog with preferred supplier items in Coupa and establish punch-out catalogs for top 3 suppliers to drive compliance and reduce maverick buying

plan.expected_impact: Consolidation of $10,804,723 tail spend into 3-5 strategic suppliers is expected to deliver $1,620,708 to $2,160,971 in annual savings (15-20% reduction) plus $300,000-400,000 in reduced processing costs from eliminating 90-100 suppliers.
kpis: Reduce active Copper wire & bar suppliers from 161 to 60-70 within 6 months
Increase top 5 supplier concentration from current ~40% to 75-80% of category spend
Realize $1,900,000+ in total savings (price reduction plus transaction cost avoidance) on $55,068,810 category spend
Reduce average PO processing cost by eliminating 500+ annual transactions with tail suppliers
risks: Supply continuity risk if tail suppliers serve niche specifications or geographies not covered by strategic suppliers (mitigate through 25-30 supplier retention for specialty needs)
Supplier push-back or capacity constraints from preferred suppliers absorbing $10.8M additional volume (validate capacity in RFQ phase)
Internal stakeholder resistance from engineering or plant buyers with established tail supplier relationships (require AVL compliance and executive sponsorship)
ERP system complexity with 5 platforms requiring coordinated supplier blocking and master data changes (dedicate ERP team and use phased rollout)
Short-term price increases if preferred suppliers lack competitive tension (maintain 3-5 approved sources and annual rebid mechanism)
erp_actions: SAP: Set posting block in LFA1 (general) and LFB1 (company code) for 90-100 tail suppliers; create source lists (ME01) designating 3-5 preferred suppliers as fixed sources with validity dates

Oracle EBS: Update supplier status to 'Inactive' for tail suppliers in Supplier Master; configure Approved Supplier List (ASL) with preferred suppliers and set 'No' for blanket approval on non-preferred vendors
Dynamics 365: Change supplier account status to 'On Hold' for tail suppliers; configure procurement categories with preferred vendor associations and approval workflows for exceptions
NetSuite: Inactivate tail supplier records; create item-supplier relationships limiting copper wire & bar items to approved vendors only in subsidiary purchase records

Coupa: Deactivate tail supplier records and remove from forms; publish preferred supplier catalogs with contracted items and pricing; configure approval rules to flag PRs for non-preferred suppliers above $5,000

Cross-ERP: Extend payment terms with preferred suppliers from standard Net 30 to Net 60-90 (SAP payment terms in LFB1, Oracle payment terms in supplier sites, similar updates in D365/NetSuite/Coupa) to improve working capital by ~$1.8M
